title: The normalized section class intertwines multiplication endomorphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be any morphism of schemes, $F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module, $I$ an injective resolution of $F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], $p\in\mathbb N$, and $V\subset S$ any open. Put $U=f^{-1}V$, $M=F|_U$, $C=H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], and $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(S,V)$ the restriction of $f$ followed by the canonical chart. Given any augmentation-preserving restricted resolution section data $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices], write $c:C(M)\to\Gamma(V,R^p f_*F)$ for resolutionSectionClass followed by evaluation of the inverse $I.\mathrm{isoRightDerivedObj}(f_*,p)$. For $a\in\Gamma(S,V)$ put $b=h^\sharp((\Gamma\operatorname{Spec}\mathrm{Iso})^{-1}(a))\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and let $\mu_b:M\to M$ be multiplication by $b$. For every $x\in C(M)$, $c(C(\mu_b)(x))=a\,c(x)$. No affineness, quasi-coherence, compactness or Ext comparison is assumed.

source.place: Tags 01E4 and 01E5; multiplication naturality of the cocycle-to-homology-sheaf map

proof.text: For a in Gamma(S,V), the canonical chart and GammaSpecIso cancel, so the displayed b is the section pullback along f followed by restriction to U. On R.resolution lift multiplication by b on M. Multiplication on the restricted original resolution gives another lift of the same endomorphism; the augmentation equation identifies them on M. The comparison theorem for injective resolutions makes these lifts homotopic, so they induce equal cohomology endomorphisms. R.components identifies their section-complex maps and naturality of isoRightDerivedObj identifies the derived endomorphism with C(mu_b).

On sections over V of the direct-image complex the endomorphism just described is multiplication by a. Exact evaluation and the homology comparison preserve that endomorphism. The presheaf module morphism sectionCohomologyTheta and the inverse sheaf-module resolution comparison are linear on V, hence preserve multiplication by a. Composing these identities gives c(C(mu_b)(x))=a*c(x). Degree zero is ordinary multiplication on sections, and empty opens or zero modules give the zero identity.
